question: Do repeat customers spend more per order than one-time customers?

semantic.answer:
## Repeat customers actually spend **less** per order, not more

Using **revenue** (item price + freight) divided by **orders**, grouped by whether the customer is a repeat buyer:

| Customer type | Orders | Revenue (BRL) | Avg. order value (BRL) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| One-time customers | 92,208 | 14,851,802.69 | **161.07** |
| Repeat customers | 6,118 | 890,977.11 | **145.63** |

*(A small residual of 1,115 orders with no matched customer profile is excluded — negligible.)*

**Takeaway:** one-time customers have a higher average order value (~R$161) than repeat customers (~R$146), a difference of about R$15, or ~10%. So in this dataset, being a repeat customer is not associated with spending more per order — if anything, slightly less. Note this uses *revenue* (includes freight); the pattern is similar in direction using product-only revenue since freight scales with order size in both groups.

Also worth noting: repeat customers are a small share of the base — only 6,118 out of the customers with valid orders, versus 92,208 one-time customers.
semantic.reason: Matches figures: one-time 161.07, repeat 145.63, correct ranking.

**No — repeat customers actually spend slightly *less* per order** (~R$145 vs ~R$161), not more. The difference is modest (~9-10%), but one-time customers have higher average order values in this dataset.
